Gas & Eye Irritation: Causes & Remedies | ASG Eye Hospital

Exposure to smoke, pollution, chemical fumes, and gas leaks can irritate the eyes and affect daily comfort. 

Common symptoms include:

• Wear protective eyewear in high-risk environments

If symptoms persist, worsen, or affect your vision, seek professional eye care promptly.

LASIK vs Contact Lenses – Which is Better for Students? | ASG Eye Hospital

Students today spend long hours studying, attending classes, using digital devices, and participating in sports or extracurricular activities. Clear vision is essential, making many students choose between contact lenses and LASIK surgery.

Contact lenses offer temporary vision correction, but they require daily cleaning, proper hygiene, and ongoing maintenance. Extended wear can sometimes lead to dryness, irritation, and an increased risk of eye infections.

LASIK surgery, on the other hand, provides long-term vision correction and reduces dependence on glasses or contact lenses. For eligible students with a stable eye prescription, 

LASIK offers several advantages:

• Freedom from daily lens maintenance
• No recurring costs for lenses and solutions
• Greater convenience during sports and activities
• Improved comfort during long study sessions
• Reduced dependence on vision correction accessories

Modern LASIK eye surgery uses advanced diagnostic technology to create personalized treatment plans with high precision and safety. Most students can return to their routine within a few days.

Best Eye Specialist for Retina Problems | ASG Eye Hospital

The retina plays a vital role in vision, yet many retinal conditions develop silently and may not show symptoms until significant damage has occurred. Early diagnosis by a retina specialist can help protect vision and improve treatment outcomes.

Warning signs that need immediate attention:

• Sudden flashes of light
• New or increasing floaters
• Blurred or distorted vision
• A dark curtain or shadow in vision
• Difficulty reading or recognising faces
• Sudden vision loss

Common retina disorders include diabetic retinopathy, retinal detachment, macular degeneration, macular holes, and retinal tears. Many of these conditions respond better when diagnosed and treated early.

At ASG Eye Hospital, advanced retinal imaging and modern diagnostic technology help specialists detect retinal problems accurately and recommend the most appropriate retina treatment.

Available treatment options may include:

• Retinal laser treatment
• Intravitreal injections
• Vitrectomy surgery
• Retinal detachment repair
• Ongoing retinal monitoring

Delaying treatment can increase the risk of permanent vision loss. If you notice any sudden changes in your eyesight, seeking prompt evaluation from a qualified retina specialist is essential.

Book your retina consultation at ASG Eye Hospital today and take the first step toward protecting your vision.

Diabetes can affect your eyesight without obvious warning signs. Many people with diabetic eye disease experience no symptoms until retinal damage has already begun. Regular eye examinations are essential for protecting long-term vision.

Common symptoms to watch for include:

• Blurred or fluctuating vision
• Floaters or dark spots
• Difficulty reading
• Distorted vision
• Poor night vision
• Sudden vision changes

One of the most common diabetes-related eye conditions is diabetic retinopathy, which affects the blood vessels in the retina. Early detection through retinal screening can help prevent serious vision complications.

Protect your eye health by:

• Maintaining healthy blood sugar levels
• Monitoring blood pressure regularly
• Taking medications as prescribed
• Staying physically active
• Avoiding tobacco use
• Scheduling regular eye check-ups

At ASG Eye Hospital, advanced diagnostic technology and experienced specialists help identify early signs of retinal damage and provide timely retina treatment when needed.
Don't wait for symptoms to appear. Regular diabetic eye care and routine retinal examinations can help preserve your vision and support better eye health.

Diabetes doesn't just affect your blood sugar—it can silently damage your eyes too.
High blood sugar can weaken and damage the tiny blood vessels of the retina, leading to diabetic retinopathy, one of the leading causes of vision loss. People with diabetes are also at a higher risk of developing cataracts at an earlier age.
The good news? Early detection and timely treatment can help prevent serious vision problems. Regular eye check-ups, good sugar control, and prompt intervention can protect your eyesight for years to come.
Don't wait for symptoms to appear. Protect your vision before it's too late.
Dr. Rahul K. Surti
Consultant Ophthalmologist
Specialist in Cataract, Retina & Advanced Eye Surgery

Dry Eye Disease (DED), commonly known as Dry Eye Syndrome, is one of the most frequently diagnosed eye conditions today. Increased screen time, prolonged exposure to air conditioning, pollution, aging, and certain medical conditions have made dry eyes increasingly common, especially in urban cities like Mumbai. While many people ignore symptoms such as burning, irritation, watering, and blurred vision, untreated dry eyes can lead to infections, corneal damage, and vision problems.
This article explains the causes, symptoms, risks, prevention strategies, and the latest dry eye treatment options available to help patients maintain healthy, comfortable vision.

Ever wondered what the (+) and (-) signs in your eye prescription mean?
A (-) number indicates Myopia (Nearsightedness) – you can see nearby objects clearly, but distant objects appear blurry.
A (+) number indicates Hyperopia (Farsightedness) – you may have difficulty focusing on nearby objects, while distant vision is usually clearer.
The higher the number, the stronger the lens power needed to correct your vision. Understanding your prescription helps you make informed decisions about your eye care.
Dr. Rahul Surti,
 Sion, Mumbai

Sudden loss of vision is a medical emergency and should never be ignored. It can occur due to conditions such as retinal detachment, retinal vein or artery blockage, eye stroke, severe glaucoma, optic nerve disorders, diabetic eye disease, or bleeding inside the eye.
Early diagnosis and timely treatment can help save vision and prevent permanent damage. If you experience sudden blurring, darkness, flashes of light, floaters, or complete vision loss, seek immediate ophthalmic care.
Dr. Rahul Surti, Advanced Eye Surgeon, Mumbai

Tunnel vision in advanced glaucoma can silently steal your side vision — often without early warning signs. By the time symptoms become noticeable, permanent optic nerve damage may already have occurred.
Don’t ignore:
* Difficulty seeing from the sides
* Bumping into objects frequently
* Trouble driving at night
* Gradual narrowing of vision
Early glaucoma detection can help protect your eyesight and prevent irreversible vision loss.

Red, itchy, watery eyes in children can spread quickly — especially in schools and daycares. Simple habits can help prevent conjunctivitis (eye flu):
• Teach children to wash hands frequently
• Avoid touching or rubbing the eyes
• Do not share towels, handkerchiefs, pillows, or eye drops
• Keep infected children at home until recovery
• Maintain good hygiene and clean surroundings
Early care and prevention can protect the whole family from infection.
-Dr. Rahul Surti, Eye Surgeon, Mumbai.

Choose:

Balanced diet rich in Vitamin A & Omega-3

Excessive screen time without breaks

Ignoring dryness, redness, or strain
Using unprescribed eye drops
Small changes today can protect your vision for years to come. Take care of your eyes—they work for you 24/7.
